findings.evidence: '## Lane capability block, lenses and refusals' (lines 236-299) gives skill-role, lens-note and refusal-reason tables and estimate arithmetic ('UTF-8 bytes ... divided by 4, rounded up'). The scripts (dispatch-reviewer, capability-block) do this work, so the orchestrator never acts on most of it.
findings.fix: Keep only what the orchestrator acts on in SKILL.md: exit 65 means a refusal, so quote the record and switch no lane, and edit-lens-pass is owner-started. Move the role, note and reason tables and the estimate rule to references/cross-ai-dispatch.md#lane-capabilities, with a 'read when a refusal or lens note must be explained' trigger, and record the move.

findings.evidence: SKILL.md is 580 lines, over the 500-line progressive-disclosure limit. Long inline blocks remain: the capability and refusal tables (236-299), the Step 1 subprocess bullet (361-425) and the Step 4 classify paragraph (502).
findings.fix: Move the lane capability and refusal detail (lines 236-299) into references/cross-ai-dispatch.md#lane-capabilities. Move the per-exit-code handling prose in Step 1 (lines 398-418) into references/cross-ai-dispatch.md#step-1-subprocess-dispatch--full-rationale-for-dispatch-reviewer, leaving one routing line per exit code (65, 69, 75, other) with its read trigger. That brings SKILL.md under 500 lines.

findings.evidence: 'MANDATORY — READ ENTIRE FILE, on every run' loads cross-ai-dispatch.md (439 lines). Step 1 and Step 3 add further mandatory full reads (reviewer-prompts.md, apply-findings.md, ../ai-kit-cross-ai/SKILL.md sections 4, 6 and 8). A routine native-only run therefore loads well over 1,000 lines.
findings.fix: Split cross-ai-dispatch.md so that points 0-2 (paths, RUN_TMP_DIR, session-default list), which every run needs, sit in their own short file read every run. Gate points 3-6 behind 'read only on the active cross-AI path (not --no-cross-ai)'.

findings.evidence: The Process pattern fits, with phased steps and checkpoints, but the core loop (Steps 1-5) carries long run-on rule paragraphs (for example line 502: 'Classify first. Whenever the Fix Summary lists...'). There is no per-iteration checklist, so the ordering is hard to follow.
findings.fix: Add a short per-iteration checklist at the top of ## Loop (ping-lanes -> dispatch each entry -> check-fold-step -> merge-reports -> parse Status -> fix route -> classify -> surface), each item linking to its step. Move the long conditional prose into references/lane-failure.md.

findings.evidence: The '## NEVER (hard landmines)' section lists only two items and defers to the Hard rules table. Other landmines are scattered through the steps and never collected: 'Never drop the file from --files', 'never render the command yourself', 'never move on to Step 1.5 while one runs'.
findings.fix: Collect the scattered landmines into the NEVER section, one line each with its reason: never drop a --files path to dodge a path_outside_roots refusal (the review would ground on less than the plan cites), never render the runner argv by hand, never read an iter<N>-<key>.md before its .exit file exists (a partial report parses as a missing Status).

findings.evidence: The description gives WHAT, WHEN and keywords but no boundaries. Near-miss neighbours (ai-kit-spec-config, PR or code review, plan execution, skill-judge) appear as negatives in evals/trigger-queries.json, yet the description never excludes them.
findings.fix: Reviews and fixes design, spec, requirements and plan documents in a loop with clean-context reviewer subagents, routing fixes to the framework's own handler (native skill, slash command or a direct-edit fixer) until approved or the iteration cap. Framework-aware across superpowers, GSD, OpenSpec, Spec Kit, Kiro, BMAD and generic RFCs, worktree-aware and scoped to the lifecycle stage, with optional cross-AI reviewers (--cross-ai/--no-cross-ai). Use when asked to review, check or iterate on a spec, plan, PLAN.md, design doc, proposal or RFC before implementing, even without the skill name, or when given document path(s) for review. Not for code or PR diff review, configuring reviewer lanes (ai-kit-spec-config), executing a plan, or scoring a SKILL.md.

findings.evidence: 'Staleness: a cached profile for a known-to-drift framework (bmad, gsd) older than ~180 days is a refresh candidate — you may re-research'. This is a menu with no default for a cache refresh that changes what reviewers are told.
findings.fix: State a default: refresh the cache copy of a bmad or gsd profile older than 180 days before using it, unless the user passed a framework override; otherwise use the cache as is.

findings.evidence: There are 19 evals with verifiable assertions, but none covers the two failure modes SKILL.md calls most common: a document in an isolated worktree (Step 0.1, 0 matches for 'worktree') and the lifecycle-stage gap guard (Step 0.6, 0 matches for 'stage' or 'intent').
findings.fix: Add an eval whose plan lives under .worktrees/<name>/, with the assertion that CODEBASE_ROOT passed to dispatch-reviewer is that worktree's toplevel. Add a GSD eval with only NN-CONTEXT.md present and a request to 'review the plan', with the assertion that the Insufficient-info stop message is surfaced and no reviewer is dispatched.

findings.evidence: 'Today only Claude Code selects a model per call (its sonnet, opus, haiku and fable aliases)'. Line 204 adds 'Fixer model: sonnet on Claude Code'. Both are version-sensitive vendor facts with no source URL or check date, and no instruction reads them live.
findings.fix: Read the alias list live from RUNTIMES (ai_kit_spec/detection.py native_selectors, for example via `python3 "$TOOLS_PY" detect-current-runtime`), or cite the Claude Code Agent tool documentation URL and the date checked next to the alias list.

findings.evidence: Step 4's single-paragraph classify rule interleaves the re-pass limit, the owner, fixer and reviewer_wrong outcomes and the fallback when jev is absent. Following the 'Escalation Required with only reviewer_wrong items' branch means cross-reading Step 5's Escalation and Cap rows to find the message shape.
findings.fix: Turn the Step 4 classify rule into a decision table (columns: fixer Status x classify result {fixer items, owner items, all reviewer_wrong, nonzero exit or jev absent} -> next action and Step 5 row), so each branch resolves without cross-reading.

findings.evidence: The Evidence section credits owner directives. That is a credit line, but docs/audit/upstream-sources.json does not exist under the root, so no registry check applies.
findings.fix: No change needed to the credit lines. If an upstream-sources registry is added later, add a row for this skill.
